The as-cast BAZ531 alloy was prepared under the atmosphere of mixed gas (V SF6 : V CO2 = 1:99) by gravity casting.
The as-cast alloy was homogenized at 450 ◦C for 12 h [17].

Subsequently, it was extruded into a bar by the DT extrusion using an XJ-500 horizontal extruder with an extrusion ratio of 278:1 and a die-exit speed of 83 m/min. Here, the temperature of the extrusion die was set as 300 ◦C. The as-homogenized alloy was heated to 400 ◦C and kept for 1 h.
As a benchmark, the ET extrusion was also conducted at 400 ◦C with the same extrusion ratio and die-exit speed.

Through the DT extrusion approach, the BAZ531-DT alloy for the first time was successfully extruded at 83 m/min showing a good surface quality.

In this series alloys, Bi reacts with Mg to produce thermally stable Mg3Bi2 (melting point of ~823 ◦C), which further prevents the generation of hot cracks at high extrusion speeds. On the other hand, fine Mg3Bi2 phases segregate grain boundaries (GBs) to hinter their motion to a great extent, delaying the growth of grains to some extent and maintaining the alloy strength.

mechanisms.name: discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX) via grain boundary bulging

evidence.quote: Fig. 7 shows the GB bulging nucleation of the DDRX mechanism. Two typical regions are highlighted in Fig. 7a and d, where fine grains are distributed at the GB in the ET and DT extrusion billets.

The DT process refined the average grain size to 15.2 μm, 0.6 times that of the equal-thermal (ET) extruded alloy, by delaying dynamic recrystallization due to a lower temperature increase.
